10014554.p001.s001.text: Genome-wide analysis of the laccase (LAC) gene family in Aeluropus littoralis: A focus on identification, evolution and expression patterns in response to abiotic stresses and ABA treatment

10014554.p002.s001.text: Laccases are plant enzymes with essential functions during growth and development.

10014554.p002.s002.text: These monophenoloxidases are involved in lignin polymerization, and their expression respond to environmental stress.

10014554.p002.s003.text: However, studies of laccases in some plants and fungi have highlighted that many structural and functional aspects of these genes are still unknown.

10014554.p002.s004.text: Here, the laccase gene family in Aeluropus littoralis (AlLAC) is described based on sequence structure and expression patterns under abiotic stresses and ABA treatment.

10014554.p002.s005.text: Fifteen non-redundant AlLACs were identified from the A. littoralis genome, which showed differences in physicochemical characteristics and gene structure.

10014554.p002.s006.text: Based on phylogenetic analysis, AlLACs and their orthologues were classified into five groups.

10014554.p002.s007.text: A close evolutionary relationship was observed between LAC gene family members in rice and A. littoralis.

10014554.p002.s008.text: According to the interaction network, AlLACs interact more with proteins involved in biological processes such as iron incorporation into the metallo-sulfur cluster, lignin catabolism, regulation of the symbiotic process and plant-type primary cell wall biogenesis.

10014554.p002.s009.text: Gene expression analysis of selected AlLACs using real-time RT (reverse transcription)-PCR revealed that AlLACs are induced in response to abiotic stresses such as cold, salt, and osmotic stress, as well as ABA treatment.

10014554.p002.s010.text: Moreover, AlLACs showed differential expression patterns in shoot and root tissues.

10014554.p002.s011.text: Our findings indicate that AlLACs are preferentially involved in the late response of A. littoralis to abiotic stress.

10014554.p004.s001.text: Laccases (EC 1.10.3.2), named after their presence in the Japanese lacquer tree (Toxicodendron vernicifluum), are multi-copper oxidases (LMCOs).

10014554.p004.s002.text: These enzymes are involved in catalyzing the oxidation of one electron of various cellular compounds such as arylamines, phenols, and aromatic thiols.

10014554.p004.s003.text: Members of the multi-copper oxidases superfamily include ceruloplasmin, nitrite reductase, ascorbate oxidase, and ferroxidase.

10014554.p004.s004.text: Laccases have been identified in many organisms, including plants, fungi, insects, and bacteria, and are involved in a wide range of cellular processes.

10014554.p004.s005.text: Plant laccases are copper-containing glycoproteins that act as key regulators for lignin polymerization and deposition in the plant cell wall.

10014554.p004.s006.text: Laccases contain three conserved copper (Cu)-oxidase domains, which can be used to identify laccase family members.

10014554.p004.s007.text: Due to their importance, members of this gene family have been identified and analyzed in plants, including Lolium perenne, Oryza Sativa, Sorghum bicolor, Arabidopsis thaliana, Brachypodium distachyon, Zea mays, Setaria viridis , Brassica napus, Gossypium arboretum, Saccharum officinarum, Eucalyptus grandis and Pyrus bretschneideri.

10014554.p005.s001.text: According to previous studies, laccases can be involved in various cellular processes.

10014554.p005.s002.text: For instance, Liu and coworkers, reported that laccases are mostly induced in the early development stage of rice seedlings, and Simões and coworkers, showed that laccases from Setaria viridis are potentially involved in monolignol oxidation.

10014554.p005.s003.text: Moreover, the study of laccases in loblolly pine revealed that these genes are expressed mainly in immature secondary xylem, the tissue for synthesized lignin.

10014554.p005.s004.text: Lignin is critical in increasing plant vigor and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses.

10014554.p005.s005.text: Accordingly, the lignin content in the mutant line for laccases genes, LAC17 and LAC14, in Arabidopsis was decreased compared to wild-type lines, suggesting that laccases are involved in lignin polymerization and decomposition.

10014554.p005.s006.text: Also the involvement of laccases in Cleome seed coat lignification was described.

10014554.p005.s007.text: Other roles have also been suggested for laccases in plants, highlighting that the members of this gene family are involved in responding to environmental stresses.

10014554.p005.s008.text: For instance, the overexpression of OsChI1, a laccase gene from rice, sharply increased the salt and drought tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis.

10014554.p005.s009.text: In addition, copper tolerance was improved in Arabidopsis transgenic lines for the overexpressed OsLAC10, a laccase10 gene from rice.

10014554.p005.s010.text: Similarly, Cai and coworkers reported that the laccase2 gene in Arabidopsis is involved in response to abiotic stresses such as drought, and Xu et al. showed that laccase genes are induced by abiotic stresses such as low/high temperature, drought, and hormone application (ABA, MeJA, and SA) in citrus.

10014554.p005.s011.text: Based on their broad substrate spectrum and ability to depolymerize lignin, laccases moved into the focus of current research.

10014554.p005.s012.text: Furthermore they became of economic importance due to their use as bioactive component of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) sensors.

10014554.p006.s001.text: Aeluropus littoralis is a halophyte monocot model that can grow under salt and drought conditions.

10014554.p006.s002.text: A. littoralis does not have the ability to be cultivated, but as a valuable source of resistance genes, it can be used in breeding and genetic engineering programs.

10014554.p006.s003.text: The genomic resources for A. littoralis provide the opportunity to identify the key genes and molecular mechanisms of response to abiotic stresses.

10014554.p006.s004.text: Motivated by the importance of laccase genes in increasing the resistance of plants against environmental conditions, the present study analyzed the sequence structure of laccase genes as well as their regulatory systems.

10014554.p006.s005.text: In addition, the expression pattern of these genes in response to environmental stress and ABA hormone was investigated in root and shoot tissues.

10014554.p027.s001.text: In total, 15 LAC proteins in Aeluropus littoralis (AlLAC) were identified ( Tables 1 ,  S2 ).

10014554.p027.s002.text: According to their physicochemical properties, the AlLACs encoded proteins ranging from 175 (AlLAC16.1) to 648 aa (AlLAC7.3).

10014554.p027.s003.text: The pI values were predicted to be between 5.17 (AlLAC11.1) and 8.93 (AlLAC17.3); eight of the 15 AlLACs showed a pI greater than 7.0 ( Table 1 ).

10014554.p027.s004.text: Based on the instability index, four of the 15 AlLACs could be introduced as unstable proteins, while the other 11 were predicted to be stable.

10014554.p027.s005.text: In addition, most AlLAC proteins (10 of the 15) showed negative values for the GRAVY index, indicating that AlLACs are more hydrophilic.

10014554.p027.s006.text: Based on the prediction of the subcellular localization, AlLACs are predominantly located in organelles such as chloroplasts (Chlo.) and vacuoles (Vacu.) ( Table 1 ).

10014554.p027.s007.text: Overall, AlLACs showed variation based on their physicochemical properties, suggesting that they may have diverse functions.

10014554.p040.s001.text: The interaction network for AlLAC proteins was drawn based on their orthologs in the model plant, Arabidopsis.

10014554.p040.s002.text: Sks11, sks13, and SKU5 proteins, which have oxidoreductase activity, were the most similar to AlLAC11.2, AlLAC16.2, and AlLAC6 proteins, respectively ( Figure 5 ).

10014554.p040.s003.text: There were no direct interactions between the laccases themselves.

10014554.p040.s004.text: Three interaction groups were observed: the first group contained Sks11 (AT3G13390), sks13 (AT3G13400), and SKU5 (AT4G12420); the second group contained LAC7 and LAC17; and the third group contained LAC5 and LAC6.

10014554.p040.s005.text: LAC5 showed the most and strongest interactions compared to the other laccases.

10014554.p040.s006.text: Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis revealed several biological process terms; iron incorporation into metallo-sulfur cluster, lignin catabolism, regulation of symbiotic processes, plant-type primary cell wall biogenesis, and L-ascorbic acid biosynthesis were significantly linked with the LAC-interaction network ( Table S4 ).

10014554.p040.s007.text: In addition, molecular function terms including cysteine desulfurase activity, glucose-6-phosphate isomerase activity, ferrochelatase activity, copper ion binding, oxidoreductase activity, cellulose synthase (udp-forming) activity, and antioxidant activity were significantly associated with the LAC-interaction network ( Table S4 ).

10014554.p041.s001.text: Protein–protein interaction network of AlLACs using STRING server v11 based on Arabidopsis interactome data.

10014554.p043.s001.text: The upstream region of AlLAC genes was analyzed to detect putative cis-regulatory elements.

10014554.p043.s002.text: The cis-regulatory elements that are involved with stress, growth and development, phytohormones, and transcription factor (TF) site were observed in the promoter region ( Figure 6 ).

10014554.p043.s003.text: The common and unknown function of cis-regulatory elements were frequently observed upstream of AlLACs ( Figure 6A ).

10014554.p043.s004.text: Cis-regulatory elements to methyl jasmonate (MeJA) and ABA responsiveness (ABRE) were frequently detected in the promoter region ( Figure 6B ).

10014554.p043.s005.text: Moreover, acting elements related to ethylene (ERE), salicylic acid (SA), gibberellic acid (GA), and auxin responsiveness were also observed in the promoter region ( Figure 6B ), as were stress-responsive MYB elements such as as-1, an acting element involved in oxidative stress-responsive, and STRE (stress-controlled transcription factors) elements ( Figure 6C ).

10014554.p043.s006.text: Dehydration-responsive element (DRE) and MBS (MYB binding site involved in drought-inducibility) elements were also observed upstream of AlLACs ( Figure 6C ).

10014554.p043.s007.text: These results suggest that laccases probably cooperate with factors involved in stress response and are probably present in stress-dependent signaling pathways.

10014554.p046.s001.text: The expression levels of five candidate AlLAC genes (AlLAC5, AlLAC14, AlLAC16.1, AlLAC17.1, and AlLAC12.2) were investigated under ABA application in shoot and root tissues of A. littoralis ( Figure 7 ).

10014554.p046.s002.text: The AlLAC genes for real time RT-PCR analysis were selected on their mRNA abundance and salt stress inducibility reported in.

10014554.p046.s003.text: Based on their expression profile, all selected genes illustrated tissue-specific expression, and they were highly expressed in shoot tissues.

10014554.p046.s004.text: Interestingly, all studied AlLACs were sharply upregulated after 48 hours of ABA application in shoot tissues, while AlLAC14 was upregulated at all-time points of ABA application in shoot tissues.

10014554.p046.s005.text: Besides, all AlLACs showed a down-regulation after 3 h of ABA application in root tissues.

10014554.p046.s006.text: Overall, ABA may indirectly affect the expression of AlLACs in the shoot.

10014554.p047.s001.text: Expression profile of AlLAC genes under ABA treatments.

10014554.p047.s002.text: Different letters above each bar indicate a significant difference (p < 0.05) based on Tukey’s range test.

10014554.p049.s001.text: Expression patterns of five selected AlLAC genes in response to abiotic stresses – cold, osmotic (using PEG application), and salt stress – were evaluated in shoot and root tissues ( Figures 8 - 10 ).

10014554.p049.s002.text: In response to cold stress, AlLAC5 was upregulated after seven days in shoot tissues, while AlLAC14 was highly induced after 48 hours and seven days in both shoot and root tissues ( Figure 8 ).

10014554.p049.s003.text: AlLAC16.1 and AlLAC17.1 were less induced in response to cold stress, and AlLAC12.2 showed upregulation at all studied time points, especially after seven days, in root tissues.

10014554.p049.s004.text: In response to salt stress, AlLAC genes showed diverse expression patterns.

10014554.p049.s005.text: For instance, AlLAC5, AlLAC17.1, and AlLAC12.2 were upregulated in roots, while AlLAC14 showed a high upregulation in the shoot ( Figure 9 ).

10014554.p049.s006.text: Furthermore, AlLAC5, and AlLAC17.1 were upregulated in both root and shoot, suggesting that these genes are directly associated with response to salt stress.

10014554.p049.s007.text: In addition, AlLAC16.1 showed a down-regulation in root tissues at all-time points in response to salinity ( Figure 9 ).

10014554.p049.s008.text: The expression profile of AlLACs was analyzed under PEG application for induction of osmotic stress.

10014554.p049.s009.text: Interestingly, all studied genes showed an upregulation in root tissues, and high expression was recorded after 48 h ( Figure 10 ).

10014554.p049.s010.text: In shoot tissues, AlLAC14 was sharply induced after 48 hours in response to drought stress.

10014554.p049.s011.text: Overall, AlLAC14 appears to be more expressed in shoot tissues, and AlLACs are more involved in the late response of A. littoralis to abiotic stress.

10014554.p050.s001.text: Expression profile of AlLAC genes in response to cold stress.

10014554.p050.s002.text: Different letters above each bar indicate a significant difference (p < 0.05) based on Tukey’s range test.

10014554.p051.s001.text: Expression profile of AlLAC genes in response to salt stress.

10014554.p051.s002.text: Different letters above each bar indicate a significant difference (p < 0.05) based on Tukey’s range test.

10014554.p052.s001.text: Expression profile of AlLAC genes in response to osmotic stress (PEG application).

10014554.p052.s002.text: Different letters above each bar indicate a significant difference (p < 0.05) based on Tukey’s range test.

10014554.p054.s001.text: Laccases have important roles such as lignin polymerization in plants, and also contribute to resistance to environmental stresses.

10014554.p054.s002.text: Enzymes of this gene family moved into focus due to their ability to catalyze steps in bio-economy and their utilization as biosensors.

10014554.p054.s003.text: Thus far, laccases have not been studied in Aeluropus littoralis, a model plant that is highly resistant to salinity stress.

10014554.p054.s004.text: A. littoralis has a high potential in the field of resistance to abiotic stresses and serves to identify and isolate new stress-adapted genes.

10014554.p054.s005.text: In the current study, 15 AlLACs were identified from the A. littoralis genome.

10014554.p054.s006.text: Previous studies have identified 30 LACs from rice, 40 LACs from the pear genome, 52 LACs from the Setaria viridis genome, 54 LACs from the Eucalyptus grandis genome, 29 LACs from the Brachypodium distachyon genome, 17 LACs from the Arabidopsis thaliana genome, and 27 LACs from the Sorghum bicolor genome.

10014554.p054.s007.text: The lower number of laccase genes found here suggests that the laccase gene family is probably less extended in A. littoralis during evolutionary processes.

10014554.p054.s008.text: Based on their physicochemical characteristics and gene structure, AlLACs were diverse, indicating that the members of this gene family are involved in various cellular processes.

10014554.p054.s009.text: Intron/exon number was also diverse among AlLACs.

10014554.p054.s010.text: It was stated that the number of exons/introns can affect the expression levels; genes with fewer exons can be rapidly activated.

10014554.p054.s011.text: According to phylogenetic analysis, LAC gene family members from A. littoralis, Arabidopsis, and rice were grouped into five classes, and a close evolutionary process was observed between AlLACs and their orthologues in rice.

10014554.p054.s012.text: This finding suggests that mutations have occurred in coding sequence regions after the divergence between dicots and monocots.

10014554.p054.s013.text: In addition, the distribution of conserved motifs might be associated with the diversity and function of genes from a family.

10014554.p054.s014.text: Some conserved motifs were observed in the extra-domain site – these regions can be used to identify AlLACs and their role of these proteins in stress response.

10014554.p055.s002.text: Leucine, proline, valine, phenylalanine, glycine, and alanine were identified as the amino acids that affect the interaction and function of AlLACs.

10014554.p055.s003.text: The interaction network for AlLAC proteins based on their orthologues in the model plant, Arabidopsis, suggested that laccases are probably involved in diverse cellular processes related to cellulose synthase activity and oxidoreductase activity, including iron incorporation into metallo-sulfur cluster, lignin catabolism, regulation of symbiotic processes, plant-type primary cell wall biogenesis, and L-ascorbic acid biosynthesis.

10014554.p055.s004.text: Previous studies have also stated that laccases are associated with processes related to plant cell wall components.

10014554.p055.s005.text: Notably, the weak interaction between the laccases indicates that they likely work in independent pathways.

10014554.p056.s001.text: Several classes of cis-acting elements related to response to hormones, light, abiotic and biotic stresses, growth and development processes were identified upstream of AlLAC genes, suggesting that the members of this gene family have multifunctional roles in A. littoralis.

10014554.p056.s002.text: We investigated the expression profile of five AlLAC genes in response to ABA and PEG application, cold, and salt stress using qRT-PCR.

10014554.p056.s003.text: Notably, AlLACs showed differential expression patterns in shoot and root tissues, indicating that these genes have different functions.

10014554.p056.s004.text: Our findings demonstrated that AlLAC14 is more induced in shoot tissues after 48 hours of exposure to stresses, however further molecular functional studies of this gene are recommended.

10014554.p056.s005.text: In addition, the selected AlLAC genes were upregulated in response to application of ABA hormone, a stress-dependent regulator that many signaling pathways use in response to adverse environmental conditions.

10014554.p056.s006.text: The induction of AlLAC genes after 48 hours of ABA application raises that these genes probably have some interaction with signaling pathway related to ABA.

10014554.p056.s007.text: Furthermore, the selected AlLAC genes illustrated diverse expression in response to abiotic stresses, including cold, salt, and osmotic stress.

10014554.p056.s008.text: Interestingly, these AlLACs were induced after 48 hours of exposure to stress conditions, revealing that AlLACs are associated with late response pathways of A. littoralis.

10014554.p056.s009.text: Several studies have mentioned the role of laccases in the process of lignification.

10014554.p056.s010.text: Laccases involves in lignin polymerization and can affects the lignin synthesis.

10014554.p056.s011.text: Lignin is a component of plant cell walls that plays an important role in increasing the resistance and strength of plants.

10014554.p056.s012.text: Besides, it was reported that LACs can be regulated by transcription factor MYB and be induced by abiotic stresses.

10014554.p056.s013.text: Our results suggest that laccases are involved in response to adverse conditions from direct and indirect pathways in A. littoralis.

10014554.p058.s001.text: The present study identified 15 AlLACs in the Aeluropus littoralis genome, which formed five groups based on phylogenetic analysis.

10014554.p058.s002.text: AlLACs showed high diversity in structure and physicochemical properties, suggesting that these gene family members were influenced by evolutionary pressure.

10014554.p058.s003.text: Various cis-regulatory elements were observed upstream of AlLACs, revealing that AlLACs are involved in different cell signaling pathways.

10014554.p058.s004.text: Moreover, AlLACs showed tissue-specific expression, suggesting that AlLAC genes might be associated with growth and development processes.

10014554.p058.s005.text: All of the selected AlLAC genes were induced in response to salt, osmotic, and cold stress, indicating that they can play a role in increasing the tolerance to adverse conditions.

PMC10014554.p001.text: Genome-wide analysis of the laccase (LAC) gene family in Aeluropus littoralis: A focus on identification, evolution and expression patterns in response to abiotic stresses and ABA treatment

PMC10014554.p002.text: Laccases are plant enzymes with essential functions during growth and development. These monophenoloxidases are involved in lignin polymerization, and their expression respond to environmental stress. However, studies of laccases in some plants and fungi have highlighted that many structural and functional aspects of these genes are still unknown. Here, the laccase gene family in Aeluropus littoralis (AlLAC) is described based on sequence structure and expression patterns under abiotic stresses and ABA treatment. Fifteen non-redundant AlLACs were identified from the A. littoralis genome, which showed differences in physicochemical characteristics and gene structure. Based on phylogenetic analysis, AlLACs and their orthologues were classified into five groups. A close evolutionary relationship was observed between LAC gene family members in rice and A. littoralis. According to the interaction network, AlLACs interact more with proteins involved in biological processes such as iron incorporation into the metallo-sulfur cluster, lignin catabolism, regulation of the symbiotic process and plant-type primary cell wall biogenesis. Gene expression analysis of selected AlLACs using real-time RT (reverse transcription)-PCR revealed that AlLACs are induced in response to abiotic stresses such as cold, salt, and osmotic stress, as well as ABA treatment. Moreover, AlLACs showed differential expression patterns in shoot and root tissues. Our findings indicate that AlLACs are preferentially involved in the late response of A. littoralis to abiotic stress.

PMC10014554.p004.text: Laccases (EC 1.10.3.2), named after their presence in the Japanese lacquer tree (Toxicodendron vernicifluum), are multi-copper oxidases (LMCOs). These enzymes are involved in catalyzing the oxidation of one electron of various cellular compounds such as arylamines, phenols, and aromatic thiols. Members of the multi-copper oxidases superfamily include ceruloplasmin, nitrite reductase, ascorbate oxidase, and ferroxidase. Laccases have been identified in many organisms, including plants, fungi, insects, and bacteria, and are involved in a wide range of cellular processes. Plant laccases are copper-containing glycoproteins that act as key regulators for lignin polymerization and deposition in the plant cell wall. Laccases contain three conserved copper (Cu)-oxidase domains, which can be used to identify laccase family members. Due to their importance, members of this gene family have been identified and analyzed in plants, including Lolium perenne, Oryza Sativa, Sorghum bicolor, Arabidopsis thaliana, Brachypodium distachyon, Zea mays, Setaria viridis , Brassica napus, Gossypium arboretum, Saccharum officinarum, Eucalyptus grandis and Pyrus bretschneideri.

PMC10014554.p005.text: According to previous studies, laccases can be involved in various cellular processes. For instance, Liu and coworkers, reported that laccases are mostly induced in the early development stage of rice seedlings, and Simões and coworkers, showed that laccases from Setaria viridis are potentially involved in monolignol oxidation. Moreover, the study of laccases in loblolly pine revealed that these genes are expressed mainly in immature secondary xylem, the tissue for synthesized lignin. Lignin is critical in increasing plant vigor and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses. Accordingly, the lignin content in the mutant line for laccases genes, LAC17 and LAC14, in Arabidopsis was decreased compared to wild-type lines, suggesting that laccases are involved in lignin polymerization and decomposition. Also the involvement of laccases in Cleome seed coat lignification was described. Other roles have also been suggested for laccases in plants, highlighting that the members of this gene family are involved in responding to environmental stresses. For instance, the overexpression of OsChI1, a laccase gene from rice, sharply increased the salt and drought tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis. In addition, copper tolerance was improved in Arabidopsis transgenic lines for the overexpressed OsLAC10, a laccase10 gene from rice. Similarly, Cai and coworkers reported that the laccase2 gene in Arabidopsis is involved in response to abiotic stresses such as drought, and Xu et al. showed that laccase genes are induced by abiotic stresses such as low/high temperature, drought, and hormone application (ABA, MeJA, and SA) in citrus. Based on their broad substrate spectrum and ability to depolymerize lignin, laccases moved into the focus of current research. Furthermore they became of economic importance due to their use as bioactive component of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) sensors.

PMC10014554.p006.text: Aeluropus littoralis is a halophyte monocot model that can grow under salt and drought conditions. A. littoralis does not have the ability to be cultivated, but as a valuable source of resistance genes, it can be used in breeding and genetic engineering programs. The genomic resources for A. littoralis provide the opportunity to identify the key genes and molecular mechanisms of response to abiotic stresses. Motivated by the importance of laccase genes in increasing the resistance of plants against environmental conditions, the present study analyzed the sequence structure of laccase genes as well as their regulatory systems. In addition, the expression pattern of these genes in response to environmental stress and ABA hormone was investigated in root and shoot tissues.

PMC10014554.p027.text: In total, 15 LAC proteins in Aeluropus littoralis (AlLAC) were identified ( Tables 1 ,  S2 ). According to their physicochemical properties, the AlLACs encoded proteins ranging from 175 (AlLAC16.1) to 648 aa (AlLAC7.3). The pI values were predicted to be between 5.17 (AlLAC11.1) and 8.93 (AlLAC17.3); eight of the 15 AlLACs showed a pI greater than 7.0 ( Table 1 ). Based on the instability index, four of the 15 AlLACs could be introduced as unstable proteins, while the other 11 were predicted to be stable. In addition, most AlLAC proteins (10 of the 15) showed negative values for the GRAVY index, indicating that AlLACs are more hydrophilic. Based on the prediction of the subcellular localization, AlLACs are predominantly located in organelles such as chloroplasts (Chlo.) and vacuoles (Vacu.) ( Table 1 ). Overall, AlLACs showed variation based on their physicochemical properties, suggesting that they may have diverse functions.

PMC10014554.p040.text: The interaction network for AlLAC proteins was drawn based on their orthologs in the model plant, Arabidopsis. Sks11, sks13, and SKU5 proteins, which have oxidoreductase activity, were the most similar to AlLAC11.2, AlLAC16.2, and AlLAC6 proteins, respectively ( Figure 5 ). There were no direct interactions between the laccases themselves. Three interaction groups were observed: the first group contained Sks11 (AT3G13390), sks13 (AT3G13400), and SKU5 (AT4G12420); the second group contained LAC7 and LAC17; and the third group contained LAC5 and LAC6. LAC5 showed the most and strongest interactions compared to the other laccases. Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis revealed several biological process terms; iron incorporation into metallo-sulfur cluster, lignin catabolism, regulation of symbiotic processes, plant-type primary cell wall biogenesis, and L-ascorbic acid biosynthesis were significantly linked with the LAC-interaction network ( Table S4 ). In addition, molecular function terms including cysteine desulfurase activity, glucose-6-phosphate isomerase activity, ferrochelatase activity, copper ion binding, oxidoreductase activity, cellulose synthase (udp-forming) activity, and antioxidant activity were significantly associated with the LAC-interaction network ( Table S4 ).

PMC10014554.p041.text: Protein–protein interaction network of AlLACs using STRING server v11 based on Arabidopsis interactome data.

PMC10014554.p043.text: The upstream region of AlLAC genes was analyzed to detect putative cis-regulatory elements. The cis-regulatory elements that are involved with stress, growth and development, phytohormones, and transcription factor (TF) site were observed in the promoter region ( Figure 6 ). The common and unknown function of cis-regulatory elements were frequently observed upstream of AlLACs ( Figure 6A ). Cis-regulatory elements to methyl jasmonate (MeJA) and ABA responsiveness (ABRE) were frequently detected in the promoter region ( Figure 6B ). Moreover, acting elements related to ethylene (ERE), salicylic acid (SA), gibberellic acid (GA), and auxin responsiveness were also observed in the promoter region ( Figure 6B ), as were stress-responsive MYB elements such as as-1, an acting element involved in oxidative stress-responsive, and STRE (stress-controlled transcription factors) elements ( Figure 6C ). Dehydration-responsive element (DRE) and MBS (MYB binding site involved in drought-inducibility) elements were also observed upstream of AlLACs ( Figure 6C ). These results suggest that laccases probably cooperate with factors involved in stress response and are probably present in stress-dependent signaling pathways.

PMC10014554.p046.text: The expression levels of five candidate AlLAC genes (AlLAC5, AlLAC14, AlLAC16.1, AlLAC17.1, and AlLAC12.2) were investigated under ABA application in shoot and root tissues of A. littoralis ( Figure 7 ). The AlLAC genes for real time RT-PCR analysis were selected on their mRNA abundance and salt stress inducibility reported in. Based on their expression profile, all selected genes illustrated tissue-specific expression, and they were highly expressed in shoot tissues. Interestingly, all studied AlLACs were sharply upregulated after 48 hours of ABA application in shoot tissues, while AlLAC14 was upregulated at all-time points of ABA application in shoot tissues. Besides, all AlLACs showed a down-regulation after 3 h of ABA application in root tissues. Overall, ABA may indirectly affect the expression of AlLACs in the shoot.

PMC10014554.p047.text: Expression profile of AlLAC genes under ABA treatments. Different letters above each bar indicate a significant difference (p < 0.05) based on Tukey’s range test.

PMC10014554.p049.text: Expression patterns of five selected AlLAC genes in response to abiotic stresses – cold, osmotic (using PEG application), and salt stress – were evaluated in shoot and root tissues ( Figures 8 - 10 ). In response to cold stress, AlLAC5 was upregulated after seven days in shoot tissues, while AlLAC14 was highly induced after 48 hours and seven days in both shoot and root tissues ( Figure 8 ). AlLAC16.1 and AlLAC17.1 were less induced in response to cold stress, and AlLAC12.2 showed upregulation at all studied time points, especially after seven days, in root tissues. In response to salt stress, AlLAC genes showed diverse expression patterns. For instance, AlLAC5, AlLAC17.1, and AlLAC12.2 were upregulated in roots, while AlLAC14 showed a high upregulation in the shoot ( Figure 9 ). Furthermore, AlLAC5, and AlLAC17.1 were upregulated in both root and shoot, suggesting that these genes are directly associated with response to salt stress. In addition, AlLAC16.1 showed a down-regulation in root tissues at all-time points in response to salinity ( Figure 9 ). The expression profile of AlLACs was analyzed under PEG application for induction of osmotic stress. Interestingly, all studied genes showed an upregulation in root tissues, and high expression was recorded after 48 h ( Figure 10 ). In shoot tissues, AlLAC14 was sharply induced after 48 hours in response to drought stress. Overall, AlLAC14 appears to be more expressed in shoot tissues, and AlLACs are more involved in the late response of A. littoralis to abiotic stress.

PMC10014554.p054.text: Laccases have important roles such as lignin polymerization in plants, and also contribute to resistance to environmental stresses. Enzymes of this gene family moved into focus due to their ability to catalyze steps in bio-economy and their utilization as biosensors. Thus far, laccases have not been studied in Aeluropus littoralis, a model plant that is highly resistant to salinity stress. A. littoralis has a high potential in the field of resistance to abiotic stresses and serves to identify and isolate new stress-adapted genes. In the current study, 15 AlLACs were identified from the A. littoralis genome. Previous studies have identified 30 LACs from rice, 40 LACs from the pear genome, 52 LACs from the Setaria viridis genome, 54 LACs from the Eucalyptus grandis genome, 29 LACs from the Brachypodium distachyon genome, 17 LACs from the Arabidopsis thaliana genome, and 27 LACs from the Sorghum bicolor genome. The lower number of laccase genes found here suggests that the laccase gene family is probably less extended in A. littoralis during evolutionary processes. Based on their physicochemical characteristics and gene structure, AlLACs were diverse, indicating that the members of this gene family are involved in various cellular processes. Intron/exon number was also diverse among AlLACs. It was stated that the number of exons/introns can affect the expression levels; genes with fewer exons can be rapidly activated. According to phylogenetic analysis, LAC gene family members from A. littoralis, Arabidopsis, and rice were grouped into five classes, and a close evolutionary process was observed between AlLACs and their orthologues in rice. This finding suggests that mutations have occurred in coding sequence regions after the divergence between dicots and monocots. In addition, the distribution of conserved motifs might be associated with the diversity and function of genes from a family. Some conserved motifs were observed in the extra-domain site – these regions can be used to identify AlLACs and their role of these proteins in stress response.

PMC10014554.p055.text: AlLACs also showed diverse 3D structures. Leucine, proline, valine, phenylalanine, glycine, and alanine were identified as the amino acids that affect the interaction and function of AlLACs. The interaction network for AlLAC proteins based on their orthologues in the model plant, Arabidopsis, suggested that laccases are probably involved in diverse cellular processes related to cellulose synthase activity and oxidoreductase activity, including iron incorporation into metallo-sulfur cluster, lignin catabolism, regulation of symbiotic processes, plant-type primary cell wall biogenesis, and L-ascorbic acid biosynthesis. Previous studies have also stated that laccases are associated with processes related to plant cell wall components. Notably, the weak interaction between the laccases indicates that they likely work in independent pathways.

PMC10014554.p056.text: Several classes of cis-acting elements related to response to hormones, light, abiotic and biotic stresses, growth and development processes were identified upstream of AlLAC genes, suggesting that the members of this gene family have multifunctional roles in A. littoralis. We investigated the expression profile of five AlLAC genes in response to ABA and PEG application, cold, and salt stress using qRT-PCR. Notably, AlLACs showed differential expression patterns in shoot and root tissues, indicating that these genes have different functions. Our findings demonstrated that AlLAC14 is more induced in shoot tissues after 48 hours of exposure to stresses, however further molecular functional studies of this gene are recommended. In addition, the selected AlLAC genes were upregulated in response to application of ABA hormone, a stress-dependent regulator that many signaling pathways use in response to adverse environmental conditions. The induction of AlLAC genes after 48 hours of ABA application raises that these genes probably have some interaction with signaling pathway related to ABA. Furthermore, the selected AlLAC genes illustrated diverse expression in response to abiotic stresses, including cold, salt, and osmotic stress. Interestingly, these AlLACs were induced after 48 hours of exposure to stress conditions, revealing that AlLACs are associated with late response pathways of A. littoralis. Several studies have mentioned the role of laccases in the process of lignification. Laccases involves in lignin polymerization and can affects the lignin synthesis. Lignin is a component of plant cell walls that plays an important role in increasing the resistance and strength of plants. Besides, it was reported that LACs can be regulated by transcription factor MYB and be induced by abiotic stresses. Our results suggest that laccases are involved in response to adverse conditions from direct and indirect pathways in A. littoralis.

PMC10014554.p058.text: The present study identified 15 AlLACs in the Aeluropus littoralis genome, which formed five groups based on phylogenetic analysis. AlLACs showed high diversity in structure and physicochemical properties, suggesting that these gene family members were influenced by evolutionary pressure. Various cis-regulatory elements were observed upstream of AlLACs, revealing that AlLACs are involved in different cell signaling pathways. Moreover, AlLACs showed tissue-specific expression, suggesting that AlLAC genes might be associated with growth and development processes. All of the selected AlLAC genes were induced in response to salt, osmotic, and cold stress, indicating that they can play a role in increasing the tolerance to adverse conditions.
